info.title: SKU.io — Update Catalog Pricing from a Price File
info.description: Apply a new price file to products that already exist in SKU.io — a supplier's updated wholesale/cost list, a new MSRP sheet, or any repriced list. Match each row to an existing product (SKU, supplier SKU, MPN, or barcode), diff old vs new prices, get the user's confirmation, then update supplier pricing tiers (what you pay) and/or product pricing tiers (what you charge). Use this when a supplier sends "new pricing effective <date>" or the business reprices a range; it never creates products (that is build-product-catalog).

get.summary: Resolve the supplier named on the price file to its supplier id.
Bulk-fetch the current catalog for matching and diffing. Rows include sku, mpn, barcode, default_supplier_id, default_supplier_sku, default_supplier_price, unit_cost, and type.

get.summary: Read a product's supplier links, including each link's supplier pricing tiers — this is where the account's actual tier name (e.g. "Wholesale") and current price come from.

put.summary: Write the new prices. Cost side goes in suppliers[].pricing[] (tier name + price, with operation "updateOrCreate" on EVERY entry so omitted suppliers are not unlinked); sell side goes in pricing[] (product_pricing_tier_name + price). All fields optional.

pricing.description: Sell-price tiers, each { product_pricing_tier_name, price }. Only send when the task includes updating what you charge; a supplier cost file alone should not touch these.

suppliers.description: Supplier links, each { supplier_id, operation, pricing: [{ supplier_pricing_tier_name, price }] }. Set operation "updateOrCreate" on every entry — when any entry omits operation the array is treated as the complete list and absent suppliers are UNLINKED. Tier price is required, numeric, >= 0 and < 100000; price null returns 422.
